public_rationale: The ownership part holds. CNBC reported in March 2026 that OpenAI owns no data centers (e1). Anthropic's S-1 shows its largest chip deal is a lease, the chips sit in data centers run by others, and its own capital spending was only $482 million in H1 2026 (e2). Negative cash flow holds for OpenAI, which burned $3.7bn in Q1 2026 (e4). It fails for Anthropic. Its S-1 shows $3.93bn of operating cash flow and about $3.45bn of free cash flow in H1 2026 (e3). The claim says both companies have negative cash flow, so that part is wrong for one of the two. The S-1 came out after the post, but the cash flow was already positive when he wrote. The open-source threat is a judgment and is not scored.
limitations: Anthropic's cash-flow figures come from news reports on the S-1, not the filing itself.
OpenAI's 2026 cash burn rests on leaked documents.
Anthropic's 2025 cash flow was negative (H1 2025 operating cash outflow), so a reader using older figures could reach a different view.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic own almost no assets, have negative cashflows, and their products are threatened by cheaper open-source alternatives.

statement.excerpt: The problem is that OpenAI and Anthropic don’t really have assets. They don’t own any of their data center infrastructure, the chips inside, or even their office buildings, and that’s before mentioning their negative cashflows and products under constant threat from cheaper open source alternatives.

from_speaker: OpenAI and Anthropic don't really have assets
don't own any of their data center infrastructure
products under constant threat from cheaper open source alternatives
our_interpretation: The claim describes the two companies' state when the post ran on 2026-10-06. He named no period, so the target period is 2026 up to the post date. That covers the most recent results either company had reported (Q1 2026 for OpenAI, H1 2026 for Anthropic). The Anthropic H1 figures were disclosed in its S-1 on 2026-10-26, after the post but before the evaluation date.

Plain reading of the ownership part: neither company owns, in any material way, the data centers or chips it runs on or the office buildings it uses. Leased or rented capacity, including finance-leased equipment, does not count as owned.

Plain reading of 'negative cashflows': the cash the business generates is negative. Operating cash flow, free cash flow or reported cash burn can each show this. The claim says this of both companies.
'Under constant threat from cheaper open source alternatives' is a qualitative judgment with no measure. It is not scored.
The claim is scored part by part. The ownership part and the cash-flow part are tested separately for each company.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting or filings from 2026 show neither company owns material data centers, chips or offices, and both report negative cash flow or cash burn.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Filings or credible reporting from 2026 show that either company owns material data center infrastructure or chips, or that either reported positive operating or free cash flow for its latest reported period before the post.

evidence.explanation: This supports the ownership part for OpenAI: it owns no data centers and leans on partners such as Oracle, Microsoft and Amazon.

evidence.excerpt: Broadcom's deal is a set of five-year equipment leases for hardware built on Google's TPU chips, installed in data centers operated by others for Anthropic.
evidence.explanation: This supports the ownership part for Anthropic. Its largest chip deal is a lease, the chips sit in data centers run by others, and the same article puts its own property and equipment spending at only $482 million in H1 2026.

evidence.excerpt: For first half 2026, Anthropic collected $3.93 billion in cash from operations. Its capital expenditure, the item that’s mushrooming at SpaceX, was so tiny this writer did a double take: just $482 million. As a result, Anthropic registered positive free cash flow of around $3.45 billion.
evidence.locator: section 'Anthropic’s operating basics look strong', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: This contradicts 'negative cashflows' for Anthropic. Its S-1 shows positive operating cash flow and positive free cash flow for H1 2026, the latest period it reported before the post.

evidence.explanation: This supports 'negative cashflows' for OpenAI. It burned cash in Q1 2026, the latest reported quarter found.
